name: Manufacturing plant
summary: Light-to-medium manufacturing buildings (single-story, 24–36' clear) cost more than warehouses because of heavier/reinforced slabs, higher electrical service and distribution, process utilities (compressed air, process water, exhaust), more HVAC, and larger office/support areas — MEP is 25–45% of cost. Process equipment is excluded. Public evidence is limited to an RSMeans 2019 model and contractor ranges, so the default is a derived midpoint; heavy, clean or crane-served plants need a separate estimate.

typicalSize.method: Terrapin lists light-manufacturing tilt-up at 50k–400k SF (e5); RSMeans model is 30k SF (e1). Mid 150k SF (judgment).

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: FAR ~0.23–0.39 (larger employee parking, utility yards, expansion land); mid 0.30 × 43,560 ≈ 13,000 SF/acre.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Shift-worker parking ≈ 1–2.5 spaces per 1,000 SF (judgment; much higher than distribution).

perPrimaryUnit.method: RSMeans 2019 1-story factory $108–$120/SF building only incl. contractor fees (e1); escalated to 2026 by ~40–45% (construction inflation 2019–2026) ≈ $152–$174, + ~8–10% for typical sitework ≈ $165–$190. Contractor ranges: light manufacturing $100–$220 (e2) and tilt-up light-manufacturing shell $155–$205 (e5); mid-range production with process utilities $180–$350 (e3). Mid $185 = escalated RSMeans with sitework, ≈ midpoint of e5 and the low end of e3. Low $130 ≈ C&W small distribution shell ($144, e6) less ~10% for a plain assembly box in a low-cost market. High $300 = within e3 for crane-served, heavy-power plants (above this use a process-specific estimate).

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC/OH&P; building shell, reinforced slab, office/locker/break areas (~10%), HVAC, electrical service and distribution to equipment, process-utility mains (compressed air, process water, exhaust), fire protection, and typical sitework. Excludes process equipment and its installation, cranes (optional line), cleanrooms, land, soft costs, off-site utilities and fees.

qualityTiers.method: economy = low/mid (130/185 = 0.70); premium ≈ (mid+high)/2/mid = 1.31; luxury ≈ high/mid (1.62) for heavy-process tier (e3 $250–$500).

systemSplit.method: MEP (21–28) set to 35%, the middle of Terrapin's 25–45% (e4); electrical 12% and HVAC/process exhaust 11% largest. Structure/envelope (03/05/07) 34%, interiors 8%, sitework 13%, GC 10%. Judgment — verify against a plant estimate.

lineItems.name: Process utility mains (compressed air, process water, exhaust) – allowance

cost.method: No unit-price source fetched. Allowance for distribution mains, compressor room and process-water piping excluding tools: judgment $6–$25/SF; scales with the gap between light ($100–$220) and mid-range ($180–$350) manufacturing (e2/e3).

lineItems.name: High-capacity electrical service & distribution to equipment (above warehouse level)

cost.method: Judgment: manufacturing loads of 15–40 W/SF vs ~3–5 W/SF for warehouse require larger switchgear, busway and drops; incremental $8–$30/SF.

lineItems.name: Office, locker, break and QA areas (~10% of area)

cost.method: Per SF of finished area: between vertical-building TI-basic ($45–$120) and C&W 2026 office fit-out low markets ~$108 (e23) / US avg $162 (e20); plant offices include locker/restroom plumbing.

lineItems.name: Bridge crane incl. runway (optional)

cost.method: Terrapin: cranes "$150K–$500K+ per crane" (e4); mid = midpoint. Count 2 per crane-served plant (judgment). Runway columns/foundations may add 10–20%.

lineItems.notes: Optional; turn on for metal/fabrication plants.

pctOfHard.method: Industrial A/E with process coordination 6–8% (RSMeans models carry 7% architectural fees, see e1 source) + permits, air/stormwater permits, testing, commissioning and owner overhead 6–14% (judgment).

softCosts.notes: Type-specific soft items: air permits, process engineering coordination, commissioning. Excludes process equipment procurement and financing.

design.method: Process layouts often change during design (judgment).

hard.method: Utility and electrical gear lead-time risk (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: min ≈ hard low $130 × 1.05; max ≈ hard high $300 × 1.4. Advanced/clean manufacturing ($400–$1,000+/SF per Terrapin) is out of scope.

evidence.quote: Factory, 1 Story with Concrete Block / Bearing Walls … Cost per S.F. (subtotal) $86.56 open shop … Contractor fees (25%) $21.64 … Total building cost $115.78 (open shop) / $128.71 (union)
evidence.scopeNotes: value = open-shop subtotal + 25% contractor fees ($86.56 + $21.64), architectural fee removed; high = union ($96.23 + $24.06). 30,000-SF, 20-ft story height; building only, sitework and process equipment not shown. 2019 dollars.

evidence.quote: Light manufacturing and assembly: $100–$220/SF — "standard slab, no cranes, basic HVAC"
evidence.scopeNotes: Contractor service page (© 2026); inclusions (sitework, process equipment) not stated. Low confidence.

evidence.quote: Mid-range production: $180–$350/SF, for facilities with "cranes, process utilities, and reinforced slabs." Heavy process manufacturing: $250–$500/SF
MEP systems "typically represent 25%–45% of total manufacturing construction cost"; cranes at "$150K–$500K+ per crane"
evidence.scopeNotes: Same page; used for the system split and the crane line item.

source.title: Tilt-Up Concrete Construction Cost Per Square Foot (2026)

evidence.quote: Building-type table row 'Light manufacturing' $155–$205/SF total shell, typical size 50k–400k SF
evidence.scopeNotes: Tilt-up shell basis per table note (excl. MEP/finishes, conflicting FAQ). Low confidence.

source.title: 2026 Americas Industrial Construction Cost Guide (landing page)

evidence.quote: Small projects averaged $144 psf (+3.6% YOY), medium $87 psf (+2.8% YOY), and large $78 psf (+2.3% YOY).
evidence.scopeNotes: Model 109,200-SF distribution building (size per CRE Daily); ground-up core and shell. Average of 46 Americas markets incl. Canada, Mexico, Costa Rica, so not a pure US figure.

source.title: Quarterly Construction Cost Report 2026 Third Quarter (North America)

evidence.quote: Indicative Construction Costs table (p.11), Industrial - Warehouse column, 18 U.S. city rows (Austin 75-155 … Washington, D.C. 140-225; full range 75-370).
evidence.scopeNotes: low/high here = median of the 18 U.S. city LOW values (140) and median of the HIGH values (227.5), computed by the researcher; un-weighted, coastal-heavy city sample, so above a true national average.

openQuestions: No cost-consultant or public-budget source for manufacturing buildings was fetchable; economic-development incentive filings (building cost separate from equipment) would provide better anchors.
Consider splitting into light assembly vs. heavy/crane-served vs. food processing.
